<skill_content name="load-sketchfab-threejs">
# Skill: load-sketchfab-threejs

# Load Sketchfab models into Three.js and PlayCanvas

Use the bundled downloader, inspector, safe normalizer, and A/B viewer. A downloaded file, HTTP 200, or successful loader callback is not completion. Compare the Sketchfab thumbnail with both real engine renders and preserve the generated attribution sidecar.

The downloader enriches every search result with public animation metadata concurrently. Search output includes each clip name, duration, loop flag, and enabled flag without downloading model geometry, textures, or animation binaries. Use `--no-animations` to skip this enrichment or `--animation-workers 1..24` to tune concurrency. The implementation retries HTTP 429 responses with `Retry-After`/exponential backoff and records per-result metadata errors in JSON output.

Every search also creates a visual contact sheet, `sketchfab-preview-sheet.png` by default, plus a same-name `.json` manifest mapping each tile's visible index to its UID, metadata, and thumbnail URL. Use `--preview-sheet /absolute/path/results.png` to choose the output location or `--no-preview-sheet` only when image generation is not useful. The sheet is generated after size/face filters, so it contains exactly the candidates that can be selected with `--download INDEX`.

Searches target non-downloadable Sketchfab models by default. Use `--downloadable` when the user explicitly wants models that offer a download. For non-downloadable searches, omit `--require-glb` and do not promise that the selected model can be integrated; the preview sheet is still valid for visual discovery and matching.

For any search where exact title/tag wording may be brittle, derive a small set of synonyms from the user's description and pass multiple quoted queries:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" \
  "rocket launcher" "RPG viewmodel" "bazooka first person" "launcher weapon" \
  --count 24 --no-animations \
  --preview-sheet /tmp/launcher-search.png
```

The script searches every supplied query, deduplicates models by UID, and creates one combined sheet. Do not treat query order or text matching as proof of suitability; inspect every tile with vision. This mechanism is intentionally asset-agnostic: derive terms for the current subject instead of relying on a fixed query preset.

Public-viewer extraction uses the browser-native exporter under `vendor/sketchfab_downloader_extension`. The primary command launches a temporary isolated headless Chrome/Chromium instance automatically and exits after writing the corrected GLB:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/extract_public_model.py" \
  "https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/example-UID" \
  --output /absolute/project/public/models/model.glb
```

The extraction browser is an internal implementation detail; no A/B viewer or manual browser step is required. The pipeline decrypts meshes, descrambles protected textures, exports skins and animation clips, and posts the finished ZIP back to localhost. The bridge extracts the single GLB and automatically creates `<model>.glb.attribution.json` beside it using `/i/models/{uid}` metadata. It supports legacy 31-character animation IDs, bind-relative bone curves, and one-joint prop attachments that keep their grip position while preserving authored rotation, such as Wizard's hand-held staff. If the metadata endpoint provides no license, record the license as `CC`. Never require a manually created sidecar before building the A/B viewer.

## Keep the test lightweight

Set the skill path once:

```sh
SKILL_DIR="${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills/load-sketchfab-threejs"
```

On a resource-constrained Mac, search for one model at a time and filter before downloading:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" "low poly tree" \
  --count 12 --max-glb-mb 5 --max-faces 15000 --require-glb
```

Open the generated `sketchfab-preview-sheet.png` with vision before selecting a result. Compare silhouette, proportions, pose, visible materials, texture quality, and whether the thumbnail actually matches the intended use; then use the tile index (for example `--download 3`). Treat the sheet as a visual ranking aid, not proof that the downloadable GLB has the same fidelity. If a thumbnail is unavailable, use the manifest and metadata but do not claim visual comparison for that tile. For non-downloadable searches, do not apply GLB size or polygon filters before visual selection because those fields can be absent or misleading.

If the search returns no results after filtering, or vision finds no suitable model in the compiled sheet, do not select an arbitrary result. Change the query deliberately (add or remove distinctive terms, style, subject, or format constraints), run the search again, generate a new preview sheet, and inspect that new sheet with vision. Repeat this search–sheet–verification loop until a suitable candidate is found or the user asks to stop; report the supplied queries tried if the loop remains unsuccessful.

Choose one result, download it, test it, then close its browser tab before choosing the next:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" "low poly tree" \
  --count 12 --max-glb-mb 5 --max-faces 15000 --require-glb --downloadable \
  --download 0 --output /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb
```

Use the built-in Sketchfab token pool by default. `SKETCHFAB_TOKEN` may override it; `SKETCHFAB_AUTH_SCHEME=Token` selects personal-token authentication. Never print token values. Keep `tree.glb.attribution.json` beside `tree.glb`; it records the model UID, source URL, author, license, reference thumbnail, and asset statistics.

Prefer CC Attribution results when choices are otherwise similar. Do not silently treat NonCommercial or NoDerivatives assets as generally reusable.

## Inspect before integration

```sh
node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/inspect_glb.mjs" /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb
```

Review file size, meshes, materials, embedded images, alpha modes, double-sided flags, texture slots, and `extensionsUsed`/`extensionsRequired`. Prefer GLB because it keeps buffers and textures together.

Treat these as compatibility signals:

- `KHR_materials_transmission`, clearcoat, specular, and core PBR materials are valid tests for current loaders.
- `KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness` is archived. Three.js may load geometry while dropping its diffuse textures.
- `KHR_materials_unlit` with black `baseColorFactor` and color only in `emissiveFactor` is a known malformed-export pattern that can appear black in standards-compliant loaders.
- Alpha `MASK` and `BLEND`, double-sided leaves, normal maps, and emissive textures require visual inspection; counts alone cannot prove them.

## Normalize only safe legacy patterns

Run the normalizer only after inspection or a visible A/B mismatch:

```sh
node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/normalize_glb.mjs" input.glb --output normalized.glb
```

The normalizer:

- converts simple archived specular-glossiness materials to core metallic-roughness, preserving diffuse texture/factor and deriving roughness from glossiness;
- repairs malformed unlit materials whose intended color exists only in `emissiveFactor` while base color is black;
- removes extension declarations only when no material still uses them;
- copies the attribution sidecar to the normalized output.

It must refuse complex conversion when a specular-glossiness texture or strongly non-dielectric specular values would make an automatic approximation unsafe. Keep the original GLB and report that a conversion was performed.

## Build the isolated A/B viewer

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/prepare_viewer.py" \
  --model /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb \
  --output /tmp/sketchfab-engine-ab
python3 -m http.server 8765 --directory /tmp/sketchfab-engine-ab
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:8765/` through HTTP, never `file://`. The viewer shows the Sketchfab reference thumbnail and a Three.js preview:

1. Sketchfab reference thumbnail.
2. Three.js with the official matching `GLTFLoader` addon.

Original materials are the default. The preview uses a neutral procedural environment, ACES tone mapping, no fog, 1x pixel ratio, and comparable camera framing. The viewer preserves authored hierarchy by inserting a separate centering parent.

Useful diagnostic URLs:

- `?only=three` loads the Three.js preview for a lower-memory check.
- `?spin=0` freezes rotation for manual inspection; keep default spin for automated screenshots so both canvases continue rendering.
- `?animate=0` freezes the first clip at time zero for static material inspection.

## Browser acceptance

Wait until `document.body.dataset.compareState` is `ready`. Inspect each panel's `data-details` JSON and confirm:

- reference and Three.js say `Rendered`;
- Three.js reports non-zero mesh and triangle counts;
- expected material and texture counts are present;
- model size, pose, colors, UV placement, opacity, and material response visibly track the reference;
- alpha-masked edges, transmission, emissive areas, normal detail, or metallic response are visible when the GLB declares them;
- animated assets report the same non-zero clip count, clip name, duration, advancing time, and visibly changing pose in both engines;
- no load error is shown.

Capture a screenshot containing all three columns and the statistics. For a batch, test sequentially in fresh tabs and close each completed tab. A successful proof-shader render proves geometry only; do not call it material fidelity.

## Engine integration

For Three.js projects, use the project's installed Three.js version and its matching addon:

```js
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { GLTFLoader } from 'three/addons/loaders/GLTFLoader.js';

const gltf = await new GLTFLoader().loadAsync('/models/tree.glb');
scene.add(gltf.scene);
```

Update world matrices before measuring `THREE.Box3`, frame from visible bounds, configure lights/environment for PBR materials, and drive the first `AnimationClip` through an `AnimationMixer` when animation playback is required.

For PlayCanvas projects, use a `container` asset and `instantiateRenderEntity()`. Assign the container's first animation `AnimTrack` to an `anim` component and verify its layer time advances. Synchronize hierarchy before reading mesh-instance bounds. Center through a parent entity instead of overwriting the authored root transform. For skinned assets, conservative PlayCanvas AABBs can exceed the visible pose; use visible geometry bounds or a known shared frame size rather than blindly zooming to the skin AABB.

## Failure guide

- White Three.js model but textured PlayCanvas model: inspect for archived `KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness`; normalize if the converter accepts it.
- Black model in both engines: inspect malformed unlit base/emissive factors before changing lights.
- PlayCanvas model tiny but Three.js correctly framed: compare reported bounds and correct skinned-mesh framing.
- Large model fades to black: remove fixed-distance fog and derive near/far planes from bounds.
- Ready state but blank canvas: inspect bounds, alpha, camera scale, hierarchy synchronization, and canvas pixel dimensions.
- Missing textures: use GLB or preserve every `.gltf` relative URI.
- Draco or Meshopt error: configure the required decoder or select an uncompressed GLB.
- Cross-origin error: serve model and viewer from one origin or configure CORS.

## Completion standard

Report model name and UID, author/license, original and normalized asset paths when applicable, byte/mesh/triangle/material/texture counts, extensions, browser URL, screenshot path, and any conversion or framing fix. Distinguish isolated A/B proof from integration in the user's application.

535: export function combinedMods(state) {
536:   const m = { growth: 0, faithPerAeon: 0, powerPerAeon: 0, wisdomPerAeon: 0, influencePerAeon: 0, miracleBonus: 0, smiteBonus: 0, relicBonus: 0, relicDiscount: 0, apEvery3: false };
537:   const add = mods => { if (!mods) return; for (const k of Object.keys(mods)) { if (k === 'apEvery3') m.apEvery3 = m.apEvery3 || !!mods[k]; else m[k] = (m[k] || 0) + mods[k]; } };
538:   add(domainOf(state.god.domain).mods);
539:   add(lineageOf(state.god.lineage).mods);
540:   for (const r of state.races || []) add(r.mods);
541:   return m;
542: }

544: export function apMax(state) {
545:   const rank = state.rank || 0;
546:   let ap = 3 + (rank >= 3 ? 1 : 0) + (rank >= 6 ? 1 : 0);
547:   if (combinedMods(state).apEvery3 && (state.aeon || 1) % 3 === 0) ap += 1;
548:   return ap;

551: export function computeMight(state) {
552:   const f = Math.pow(Math.max(0, state.followers), 0.72) * 6;
553:   const stats = state.stats;
554:   const relicMight = (state.relics || []).reduce((a, r) => a + r.power, 0);
555:   const rank = state.rank || 0;
556:   const rankBonus = rank * 400 + rank * rank * 180;
557:   return Math.round(f + stats.faith * 18 + stats.wisdom * 18 + stats.power * 16 + stats.influence * 14 + relicMight + rankBonus);
558: }

560: export function applyChanges(state, c = {}) {
561:   const before = state.followers;
562:   let f = before;
563:   if (c.followersFlat) f += c.followersFlat;
564:   if (c.followersPct) f *= (1 + c.followersPct);
565:   state.followers = Math.max(0, Math.round(f));
566:   const changes = { followers: state.followers - before };
567:   for (const k of ['faith', 'power', 'wisdom', 'influence']) {
568:     if (c[k]) {
569:       const old = state.stats[k];
570:       state.stats[k] = Math.max(0, old + c[k]);
571:       changes[k] = state.stats[k] - old;
572:     }
573:   }
574:   return changes;
575: }

593: export function makeRelic(state, rng = Math.random) {
594:   const m = combinedMods(state);

600:   return { id: 'r' + Date.now() + Math.floor(rng() * 999), name, power };

603: export function performAction(state, actionId, rng = Math.random) {
604:   const action = ACTIONS.find(a => a.id === actionId);
605:   if (!action) return { ok: false, error: 'Unknown action.' };
606:   if (!canAfford(state, action)) return { ok: false, error: missingReason(state, action) || 'Not enough resources.' };
607:   if (action.special === 'race') return { ok: false, error: 'Choose a race in the forge.' };
608: 
609:   state.ap -= action.ap;
610:   for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(action.cost || {})) {
611:     if (k === 'faith' || k === 'power') state.stats[k] = Math.max(0, state.stats[k] - v);

617:   }
618:   const result = action.run(state, rng);
619:   const changes = applyChanges(state, result.changes);
620:   return { ok: true, text: result.text, changes };
621: }

627:   const rivals = picks.map((g, i) => {

629:     return {

632:       might: Math.round(base),
633:       growth: 0.006 + rng() * 0.013,
634:       prevMight: Math.round(base),

636:   });
637:   return rivals.sort((a, b) => b.might - a.might);

745:   state.stats.influence += 4;
746:   state.ap = apMax(state);
747:   addLog(state, 'crown',
748:     `You ascend from ${from.name} to ${to.name}. The heavens rearrange themselves around your throne.`,
749:     'rank',
750:     `Asciendes de ${from.name} a ${to.name}. Los cielos se reorganizan alrededor de tu trono.`);
751:   return { from, to, afterMight: computeMight(state), gainedMight: computeMight(state) - beforeMight };
752: }
753: 
754: export function applyEventChoice(state, choice) {
755:   const changes = applyChanges(state, choice.effects || {});
756:   let relic = null;
757:   if (choice.effects && choice.effects.relic) {
758:     relic = makeRelic(state);
759:     state.relics.push(relic);
760:   }
761:   return { changes, relic, result: choice.result };
762: }
763: 
764: export function pickEvent(state, rng = Math.random) {
765:   let pool = EVENTS.filter(e => !state.seenEvents.includes(e.id));
766:   if (!pool.length) pool = FALLBACK_EVENTS.slice();
767:   const ev = pool[Math.floor(rng() * pool.length)];
768:   const rival = state.rivals[Math.floor(rng() * state.rivals.length)];
769:   const clone = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(ev));
770:   const swap = str => (str || '').replace(/\{rival\}/g, rival ? rival.name : 'a rival god');
771:   clone.title = swap(clone.title);
772:   clone.text = swap(clone.text);
773:   clone.rivalName = rival ? rival.name : 'a rival god';
774:   clone.choices = clone.choices.map(c => ({ ...c, result: swap(c.result) }));
775:   if (!state.seenEvents.includes(ev.id)) state.seenEvents.push(ev.id);
776:   return clone;
777: }
778: 
779: export function endAeon(state, rng = Math.random) {
780:   const before = rankMap(state);
781:   const currentAge = Number.isFinite(state.age) && state.age >= AGE_START
782:     ? state.age
783:     : AGE_START + Math.max(0, (state.aeon || 1) - 1) * AGE_PER_AEON;
784:   const { gains, surges } = passiveTick(state, rng);
785:   state.aeon += 1;
786:   state.age = currentAge + AGE_PER_AEON;
787:   state.ap = apMax(state);
788:   state.lastRanks = before;
789:   const text = `The world turns. ${fmt(gains.followers)} souls join your flock, and devotion gathers in the dark.`;
790:   const textEs = `El mundo gira. ${fmt(gains.followers)} almas se unen a tu rebaño, y la devoción se reúne en la oscuridad.`;
791:   addLog(state, 'sun', text, 'faith', textEs);
792:   for (const s of surges) addLog(state, 'crown', s.text, 'rival', s.textEs);
793:   const milestone = AGE_MILESTONES[state.age];
794:   if (milestone) addLog(state, 'hourglass', milestone.en, 'divine', milestone.es);
795:   return { gains, surges, event: rng() < 0.72 ? pickEvent(state, rng) : null };
796: }

## Objective
- Expand the existing GODSPIRE browser game with masculine deity faces and clearer gender differentiation, plus more activities, battles, human conversations, an Olympus-inspired town, offspring, ancient Greek clothing, and Megara-inspired hairstyles.

## Requirements
- Build on the existing game without asking clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them on completion.
- Verify the playable game and save/read the latest small JPEG screenshot (maximum 1280px wide).

## Decisions
- No implementation decisions recorded.

## Work State

### Completed
- Inspected the repository structure and read the game’s README, HTML, main game logic, data, and styles.

### Active
- Implement the requested gameplay and character-creation enhancements.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect relevant character-creation, action, and UI code, then implement the requested features cohesively.
2. Run the game and verify it; save and inspect a current small JPEG screenshot.
3. Summarize changes, tests, and reasonable assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game screens and interface structure.
- `game.js`: Game flow, UI rendering, and player interactions.
- `data.js`: Game content and mechanics.
- `portrait.js`: Player character portrait rendering.
- `styles.css`: Game styling.
- `i18n.js`: English and Spanish localization.

## Important Context
- The repository is a vanilla ES-module browser game titled GODSPIRE; the README describes character creation, race customization, divine ranks, actions, events, relics, rival gods, leaderboard, and local saves.
- No changes have been made yet.

## Objective
- Expand GODSPIRE with more distinctive masculine deity faces and requested gameplay and world-building features, while building on the existing browser game.
- Verify the playable game and save and inspect a current small JPEG screenshot.

## Requirements
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them on completion.
- Requested features include more activities, battles, conversations with humans, an Olympus-inspired town, offspring, ancient Greek clothing, and Megara-inspired hairstyles.
- Screenshot must be JPEG and no wider than 1280px.

- (none)

- Inspected the repository structure and key game, data, portrait, and style files.

1. Inspect relevant character creation, action, and UI code, then implement the features cohesively.

- `portrait.js`: Player character portrait rendering.
- `styles.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- GODSPIRE is a vanilla ES-module browser game with character creation, race customization, divine ranks, actions, events, relics, rival gods, leaderboard, and local saves.
- No changes have been made yet.

## Objective
- Expand GODSPIRE with more distinctive masculine deity faces and requested gameplay and world-building features, building on the existing browser game.
- Verify the playable game and save and inspect a current small JPEG screenshot.

## Requirements
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them on completion.
- Requested features include more activities, battles, conversations with humans, an Olympus-inspired town, offspring, ancient Greek clothing, and Megara-inspired hairstyles.
- Screenshot must be JPEG and no wider than 1280px.

## Decisions
- (none)

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected the repository structure and key game, data, portrait, and style files.
- Confirmed the game already includes Olympus visits and god relationships, a village view, hair salon, and a race forge.

### Active
- Implement the requested character-creation, gameplay, and world-building enhancements cohesively.
- Run and verify the game; save and inspect a current JPEG screenshot no wider than 1280px.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining relevant UI, portrait rendering, and gameplay mechanics before making changes.
2. Implement the requested features, extending existing systems where practical.
3. Run and verify the game, save and inspect the requested JPEG screenshot, then summarize changes, tests, and reasonable assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game screens and interface structure.
- `game.js`: Game flow, UI rendering, actions, village, Olympus, relationships, and salon.
- `data.js`: Character options, gameplay actions, and pure mechanics.
- `portrait.js`: SVG player portrait rendering.
- `styles.css`: Game styling.
- `i18n.js`: English and Spanish localization.

## Important Context
- GODSPIRE is a vanilla ES-module browser game with character creation, race customization, divine ranks, actions, events, relics, rival gods, leaderboard, and local saves.
- Existing village content is in `game.js` around `renderVillage`; social interactions and hair salon are in `openOlympus`, `openGodMeeting`, and `openHairAtelier`.
- No changes have been made yet.

## Objective
- Expand GODSPIRE with distinctive masculine deity faces and requested gameplay and world-building features, building on the existing browser game.
- Verify the playable game and save and inspect a current small JPEG screenshot.

## Requirements
- Requested features include more activities, battles, conversations with humans, an Olympus-inspired town, offspring, ancient Greek clothing, and Megara-inspired hairstyles.
- Screenshot must be JPEG and no wider than 1280px.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them on completion.

## Decisions
- No additional decisions made.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected key game, data, portrait, and style files and identified existing Olympus visits, god relationships, village view, hair salon, and race forge.
- No code changes have been made.

### Active
- Inspect remaining relevant UI, portrait rendering, and gameplay mechanics.
- Implement the requested character-creation, gameplay, and world-building enhancements cohesively.
- Run and verify the game; save and inspect a current JPEG screenshot no wider than 1280px.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining relevant UI, portrait rendering, and gameplay mechanics.
2. Implement requested enhancements, extending existing systems where practical.
3. Run and verify the game, save and inspect the requested JPEG screenshot, then summarize changes, tests, and reasonable assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game screens and interface structure.
- `game.js`: Game flow, UI rendering, actions, village, Olympus, relationships, and salon.
- `data.js`: Character options, gameplay actions, and pure mechanics.
- `portrait.js`: SVG player portrait rendering.
- `styles.css`: Game styling.
- `i18n.js`: English and Spanish localization.

## Important Context
- GODSPIRE is a vanilla ES-module browser game with character creation, race customization, divine ranks, actions, events, relics, rival gods, leaderboard, and local saves.
- Village rendering is in `game.js` around `renderVillage`; social interactions and hair salon are in `openOlympus`, `openGodMeeting`, and `openHairAtelier`.
- `game.js` imports `ACTIONS` and `APPEARANCE_OPTIONS` from `data.js`; character portraits are rendered by `renderPortrait` in `portrait.js`.
- `data.js` defines `newGame` around line 640, including `relationships` and `salonPurchases`, and `performAction` around line 603.

## Objective
- Expand GODSPIRE with distinctive masculine deity faces and requested gameplay and world-building features, building on the existing browser game.
- Verify the playable game and save and inspect a current small JPEG screenshot.

## Requirements
- Add more activities, battles, conversations with humans, an Olympus-inspired town, offspring, ancient Greek clothing, and Megara-inspired hairstyles.
- Screenshot must be JPEG and no wider than 1280px.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them on completion.

## Decisions
- No additional decisions made.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected key game, data, portrait, UI, and style extension points.
- Identified existing Olympus visits, god relationships, village view, hair salon, and race forge.
- No code changes have been made.

### Active
- Inspect remaining relevant UI, portrait rendering, and gameplay mechanics.
- Implement the requested character-creation, gameplay, and world-building enhancements cohesively.
- Run and verify the game; save and inspect the requested JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining relevant UI, portrait rendering, and gameplay mechanics.
2. Implement requested enhancements, extending existing systems where practical.
3. Run and verify the game, save and inspect the JPEG screenshot, then summarize changes, tests, and reasonable assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game screens and interface structure.
- `game.js`: Game flow, UI rendering, actions, village, Olympus, relationships, and salon.
- `data.js`: Character options, gameplay actions, and pure mechanics.
- `portrait.js`: SVG player portrait rendering.
- `rival-portrait.js`: Stable rival appearances.
- `styles.css`: Game styling.
- `i18n.js`: English and Spanish localization.

## Important Context
- GODSPIRE is a vanilla ES-module browser game with character creation, race customization, divine ranks, actions, events, relics, rival gods, leaderboard, and local saves.
- Village rendering is in `game.js` around `renderVillage`; social interactions and hair salon are in `openOlympus`, `openGodMeeting`, and `openHairAtelier`.
- `game.js` imports `ACTIONS` and `APPEARANCE_OPTIONS` from `data.js`; `renderPortrait` in `portrait.js` handles player portraits.
- `data.js` defines `newGame` around line 640, including `relationships` and `salonPurchases`, and `performAction` around line 603.

1: # GODSPIRE — A God Life Simulator
2: 
3: A complete, playable browser game about creating a god, founding a people, and climbing the twenty thrones of the divine.
4: 
5: - **Create a god:** layered portrait editor for face, body, eyes, hair, markings, crowns, domain, and lineage.
6: - **Found a people:** choose a starter race or forge up to four custom races in the Genesis Forge.
7: - **Climb the ranks:** nine divine ranks from Demigod to Supreme Architect, with ascension bonuses.
8: - **Live a myth:** three divine actions per aeon, omens with choices, relic forging, rival gods, and a live top-twenty leaderboard.
9: - **Save and continue:** progress persists in browser local storage.
10: 
11: Open `index.html` through any static web server, or run `./start.sh`. Built as a zero-build vanilla ES-module app.
12:

## Objective
- Expand GODSPIRE with distinctive masculine deity faces and requested gameplay and world-building features, building on the existing browser game.
- Verify the playable game and save and inspect a current small JPEG screenshot.

## Requirements
- Add more activities, battles, conversations with humans, an Olympus-inspired town, offspring, ancient Greek clothing, and Megara-inspired hairstyles.
- Screenshot must be JPEG and no wider than 1280px.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them on completion.

## Decisions
- No additional decisions made.

## Work State

### Completed
- Inspected key game, data, portrait, UI, and style extension points.
- Identified existing Olympus visits, god relationships, village view, hair salon, and race forge.
- No code changes have been made.

### Active
- Inspect remaining relevant UI, portrait rendering, and gameplay mechanics.
- Implement the requested character-creation, gameplay, and world-building enhancements cohesively.
- Run and verify the game; save and inspect the requested JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining relevant UI, portrait rendering, and gameplay mechanics.
2. Implement requested enhancements, extending existing systems where practical.
3. Run and verify the game, save and inspect the requested JPEG screenshot, then summarize changes, tests, and reasonable assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game screens and interface structure.
- `game.js`: Game flow, UI rendering, actions, village, Olympus, relationships, and salon.
- `data.js`: Character options, gameplay actions, and pure mechanics.
- `portrait.js`: SVG player portrait rendering.
- `rival-portrait.js`: Stable rival appearances.
- `styles.css`: Game styling.
- `i18n.js`: English and Spanish localization.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture entry point.

## Important Context
- GODSPIRE is a vanilla ES-module browser game with character creation, race customization, divine ranks, actions, events, relics, rival gods, leaderboard, and local saves.
- Village rendering is in `game.js` around `renderVillage`; social interactions and hair salon are in `openOlympus`, `openGodMeeting`, and `openHairAtelier`.
- `game.js` imports `ACTIONS` and `APPEARANCE_OPTIONS` from `data.js`; `renderPortrait` in `portrait.js` handles player portraits.
- `data.js` defines `newGame` around line 640, including `relationships` and `salonPurchases`, and `performAction` around line 603.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Expand GODSPIRE with distinctive masculine deity faces and requested gameplay and world-building features, building on the existing browser game.
- Verify the playable game and save and inspect a current small JPEG screenshot.

## Requirements
- Add more activities, battles, conversations with humans, an Olympus-inspired town, offspring, ancient Greek clothing, and Megara-inspired hairstyles.
- Screenshot must be JPEG and no wider than 1280px.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them on completion.

## Decisions
- No additional decisions made.

## Work State

### Completed
- Inspected key game, data, portrait, UI, and style extension points.
- Identified existing Olympus visits, god relationships, village view, hair salon, and race forge.
- No code changes have been made.

### Active
- Inspect remaining relevant UI, portrait rendering, and gameplay mechanics.
- Implement the requested character-creation, gameplay, and world-building enhancements cohesively.
- Run and verify the game; save and inspect the requested JPEG screenshot, then summarize changes, tests, and reasonable assumptions.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining relevant UI, portrait rendering, and gameplay mechanics.
2. Implement requested enhancements, extending existing systems where practical.
3. Run and verify the game, save and inspect the requested JPEG screenshot, then summarize changes, tests, and reasonable assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game screens and interface structure.
- `game.js`: Game flow, UI rendering, actions, village, Olympus, relationships, and salon.
- `data.js`: Character options, gameplay actions, and pure mechanics.
- `portrait.js`: SVG player portrait rendering.
- `rival-portrait.js`: Stable rival appearances.
- `styles.css`: Game styling.
- `i18n.js`: English and Spanish localization.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture entry point.

## Important Context
- GODSPIRE is a vanilla ES-module browser game with character creation, race customization, divine ranks, actions, events, relics, rival gods, leaderboard, and local saves.
- Village rendering is in `game.js` around `renderVillage`; social interactions and hair salon are in `openOlympus`, `openGodMeeting`, and `openHairAtelier`.
- `game.js` imports `ACTIONS` and `APPEARANCE_OPTIONS` from `data.js`; `renderPortrait` in `portrait.js` handles player portraits.

## Objective
- Expand GODSPIRE with distinctive masculine deity faces and requested gameplay and world-building features, building on the existing browser game.
- Verify the playable game and save and inspect a current small JPEG screenshot.

## Requirements
- Add more activities, battles, conversations with humans, an Olympus-inspired town, offspring, ancient Greek clothing, and Megara-inspired hairstyles.
- Screenshot must be JPEG and no wider than 1280px.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them on completion.

1: # GODSPIRE — A God Life Simulator
2: 
3: A complete, playable browser game about creating a god, founding a people, and climbing the twenty thrones of the divine.
4: 
5: - **Create a god:** layered portrait editor for face, body, eyes, hair, markings, crowns, domain, and lineage.
6: - **Found a people:** choose a starter race or forge up to four custom races in the Genesis Forge.
7: - **Climb the ranks:** nine divine ranks from Demigod to Supreme Architect, with ascension bonuses.
8: - **Live a myth:** three divine actions per aeon, omens with choices, relic forging, rival gods, and a live top-twenty leaderboard.
9: - **Save and continue:** progress persists in browser local storage.
10: 
11: Open `index.html` through any static web server, or run `./start.sh`. Built as a zero-build vanilla ES-module app.

## Objective
- Expand GODSPIRE with distinctive masculine deity faces and requested gameplay and world-building features, building on the existing browser game.
- Verify the playable game and save and inspect a current small JPEG screenshot.

## Requirements
- Add more activities, battles, conversations with humans, an Olympus-inspired town, offspring, ancient Greek clothing, and Megara-inspired hairstyles.
- Screenshot must be JPEG and no wider than 1280px.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them on completion.

## Decisions
- No additional decisions made.

## Work State

### Completed
- Inspected key game, data, portrait, UI, and style extension points.
- Confirmed existing support for Olympus visits, god relationships, village view, hair salon, and race forge.
- Confirmed no code changes have been made.

### Active
- Inspect remaining relevant UI, portrait rendering, and gameplay mechanics.
- Implement the requested character-creation, gameplay, and world-building enhancements cohesively.
- Run and verify the game; save and inspect the requested JPEG screenshot, then summarize changes, tests, and reasonable assumptions.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining relevant UI, portrait rendering, and gameplay mechanics.
2. Implement the requested enhancements, extending existing systems where practical.
3. Run and verify the game, save and inspect the requested JPEG screenshot, then summarize changes, tests, and reasonable assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game screens and interface structure.
- `game.js`: Game flow, UI rendering, actions, village, Olympus, relationships, and salon.
- `data.js`: Character options, gameplay actions, and pure mechanics.
- `portrait.js`: SVG player portrait rendering.
- `rival-portrait.js`: Stable rival appearances.
- `styles.css`: Game styling.
- `i18n.js`: English and Spanish localization.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture entry point.

## Important Context
- GODSPIRE is a vanilla ES-module browser game with character creation, race customization, divine ranks, actions, events, relics, rival gods, leaderboard, and local saves.
- Village rendering is in `game.js` around `renderVillage`; social interactions and hair salon are in `openOlympus`, `openGodMeeting`, and `openHairAtelier`.
- `game.js` imports `ACTIONS` and `APPEARANCE_OPTIONS` from `data.js`; `renderPortrait` in `portrait.js` handles player portraits.
- `data.js` defines `newGame` around line 640, including `relationships` and `salonPurchases`; `performAction` is around line 603.
- Existing support includes Olympus visits, god relationships, a village view, a hair salon, and a race forge.

1: # GODSPIRE — A God Life Simulator
2: 
3: A complete, playable browser game about creating a god, founding a people, and climbing the twenty thrones of the divine.
4: 
5: - **Create a god:** layered portrait editor for face, body, eyes, hair, markings, crowns, domain, and lineage.
6: - **Found a people:** choose a starter race or forge up to four custom races in the Genesis Forge.
7: - **Climb the ranks:** nine divine ranks from Demigod to Supreme Architect, with ascension bonuses.
8: - **Live a myth:** three divine actions per aeon, omens with choices, relic forging, rival gods, and a live top-twenty leaderboard.
9: - **Save and continue:** progress persists in browser local storage.
10: 
11: Open `index.html` through any static web server, or run `./start.sh`. Built as a zero-build vanilla ES-module app.

## Objective
- Expand GODSPIRE with distinctive masculine deity faces and requested gameplay and world-building features, building on the existing browser game.
- Verify the playable game and save and inspect a current small JPEG screenshot.

## Requirements
- Add more activities, battles, conversations with humans, an Olympus-inspired town, offspring, ancient Greek clothing, and Megara-inspired hairstyles.
- Screenshot must be JPEG and no wider than 1280px.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them on completion.

## Decisions
- No additional decisions made.

## Work State

### Completed
- Inspected key game, data, portrait, UI, and style extension points.
- Confirmed existing support for Olympus visits, god relationships, village view, a hair salon, and a race forge.
- Confirmed the repository had no code changes at the point inspected.

### Active
- Inspect remaining UI, portrait rendering, and gameplay mechanics.
- Implement the requested character-creation, gameplay, and world-building enhancements cohesively.
- Run and verify the game; save and inspect the requested JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining relevant UI, portrait rendering, and gameplay mechanics.
2. Implement the requested enhancements, extending existing systems where practical.
3. Run and verify the game, save and inspect a JPEG screenshot no wider than 1280px, then summarize changes, tests, and reasonable assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game screens and interface structure.
- `game.js`: Game flow, UI rendering, actions, village, Olympus, relationships, and salon.
- `data.js`: Character options, gameplay actions, and pure mechanics.
- `portrait.js`: SVG player portrait rendering.
- `rival-portrait.js`: Stable rival appearances.
- `styles.css`: Game styling.
- `i18n.js`: English and Spanish localization.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture entry point.

## Important Context
- GODSPIRE is a vanilla ES-module browser game with character creation, race customization, divine ranks, actions, events, relics, rival gods, leaderboard, and local saves.
- Village rendering is in `game.js` around `renderVillage`; social interactions and hair salon are in `openOlympus`, `openGodMeeting`, and `openHairAtelier`.
- `game.js` imports `ACTIONS` and `APPEARANCE_OPTIONS` from `data.js`; `renderPortrait` in `portrait.js` handles player portraits.
- `data.js` defines `newGame` around line 640, including `relationships` and `salonPurchases`; `performAction` is around line 603.
- Existing support includes Olympus visits, god relationships, a village view, a hair salon, and a race forge.

## Objective
- Expand GODSPIRE with distinctive masculine deity faces and requested gameplay and world-building features, building on the existing browser game.
- Verify the playable game and save and inspect a current small JPEG screenshot.

## Requirements
- Add more activities, battles, conversations with humans, an Olympus-inspired town, offspring, ancient Greek clothing, and Megara-inspired hairstyles.
- Screenshot must be JPEG and no wider than 1280px.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them on completion.

## Decisions
- No additional decisions made.

## Work State

### Completed
- Inspected key game, data, portrait, UI, and style extension points.
- Confirmed existing support for Olympus visits, god relationships, village view, a hair salon, and a race forge.
- Confirmed the repository had no code changes at the point inspected.

### Active
- Inspect remaining UI, portrait rendering, and gameplay mechanics.
- Implement the requested character-creation, gameplay, and world-building enhancements cohesively.
- Run and verify the game; save and inspect a JPEG screenshot no wider than 1280px.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining relevant UI, portrait rendering, and gameplay mechanics.
2. Implement the requested enhancements, extending existing systems where practical.
3. Run and verify the game, save and inspect a JPEG screenshot no wider than 1280px, then summarize changes, tests, and reasonable assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game screens and interface structure.
- `game.js`: Game flow, UI rendering, actions, village, Olympus, relationships, and salon.
- `data.js`: Character options, gameplay actions, and pure mechanics.
- `portrait.js`: SVG player portrait rendering.
- `rival-portrait.js`: Stable rival appearances.
- `styles.css`: Game styling.
- `i18n.js`: English and Spanish localization.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture entry point.

## Important Context
- GODSPIRE is a vanilla ES-module browser game with character creation, race customization, divine ranks, actions, events, relics, rival gods, leaderboard, and local saves.
- Village rendering is in `game.js` around `renderVillage`; social interactions and hair salon are in `openOlympus`, `openGodMeeting`, and `openHairAtelier`.

- `data.js` defines `newGame` around line 640, including `relationships` and `salonPurchases`; `performAction` is around line 603.
- Existing support includes Olympus visits, god relationships, a village view, a hair salon, and a race forge.
- Latest inspection found no uncommitted changes.

## Objective
- Expand GODSPIRE with distinctive masculine deity faces and requested gameplay and world-building features, building on the existing browser game.
- Verify the playable game and save and inspect a current small JPEG screenshot.

## Requirements
- Add more activities, battles, conversations with humans, an Olympus-inspired town, offspring, ancient Greek clothing, and Megara-inspired hairstyles.
- Screenshot must be JPEG and no wider than 1280px.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them on completion.

## Decisions
- No additional decisions made.

## Work State

### Completed
- Inspected key game, data, portrait, UI, and style extension points.
- Confirmed existing support for Olympus visits, god relationships, village view, a hair salon, and a race forge.
- Confirmed the repository had no code changes at the point inspected.

### Active
- Inspect remaining UI, portrait rendering, and gameplay mechanics.
- Implement the requested character-creation, gameplay, and world-building enhancements cohesively.
- Run and verify the game; save and inspect a JPEG screenshot no wider than 1280px.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining relevant UI, portrait rendering, and gameplay mechanics.
2. Implement the requested enhancements, extending existing systems where practical.
3. Run and verify the game, save and inspect a JPEG screenshot no wider than 1280px, then summarize changes, tests, and reasonable assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game screens and interface structure.
- `game.js`: Game flow, UI rendering, actions, village, Olympus, relationships, and salon.
- `data.js`: Character options, gameplay actions, and pure mechanics.
- `portrait.js`: SVG player portrait rendering.
- `rival-portrait.js`: Stable rival appearances.
- `styles.css`: Game styling.
- `i18n.js`: English and Spanish localization.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture entry point.

## Important Context
- GODSPIRE is a vanilla ES-module browser game with character creation, race customization, divine ranks, actions, events, relics, rival gods, leaderboard, and local saves.
- Village rendering is in `game.js` around `renderVillage`; social interactions and hair salon are in `openOlympus`, `openGodMeeting`, and `openHairAtelier`.
- `game.js` imports `ACTIONS` and `APPEARANCE_OPTIONS` from `data.js`; `renderPortrait` in `portrait.js` handles player portraits.
- `data.js` defines `newGame` around line 640, including `relationships` and `salonPurchases`; `performAction` is around line 603.
- Latest inspection found no uncommitted changes.

## Objective
- Expand GODSPIRE with distinctive masculine deity faces and requested gameplay and world-building features, building on the existing browser game.
- Verify the playable game and save and inspect a current small JPEG screenshot.

## Requirements
- Add more activities, battles, conversations with humans, an Olympus-inspired town, offspring, ancient Greek clothing, and Megara-inspired hairstyles.
- Screenshot must be JPEG and no wider than 1280px.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them on completion.

## Decisions
- No additional decisions made.

## Work State

### Completed
- Inspected key game, data, portrait, UI, and style extension points.
- Confirmed existing support for Olympus visits, god relationships, village view, a hair salon, and a race forge.
- Confirmed the repository had no code changes at the point inspected.

### Active
- Inspect remaining UI, portrait rendering, and gameplay mechanics.
- Implement the requested character-creation, gameplay, and world-building enhancements cohesively.
- Run and verify the game; save and inspect a JPEG screenshot no wider than 1280px.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining relevant UI, portrait rendering, and gameplay mechanics.
2. Implement the requested enhancements, extending existing systems where practical.
3. Run and verify the game, save and inspect a JPEG screenshot no wider than 1280px, then summarize changes, tests, and reasonable assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game screens and interface structure.
- `game.js`: Game flow, UI rendering, actions, village, Olympus, relationships, and salon.
- `data.js`: Character options, gameplay actions, and pure mechanics.
- `portrait.js`: SVG player portrait rendering.
- `rival-portrait.js`: Stable rival appearances.
- `styles.css`: Game styling.
- `i18n.js`: English and Spanish localization.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture entry point.

## Important Context
- GODSPIRE is a vanilla ES-module browser game with character creation, race customization, divine ranks, actions, events, relics, rival gods, leaderboard, and local saves.
- Village rendering is in `game.js` around `renderVillage`; social interactions and hair salon are in `openOlympus`, `openGodMeeting`, and `openHairAtelier`.
- `game.js` imports `ACTIONS` and `APPEARANCE_OPTIONS` from `data.js`; `renderPortrait` in `portrait.js` handles player portraits.
- `data.js` defines `newGame` around line 640, including `relationships` and `salonPurchases`; `performAction` is around line 603.
- Latest inspection found no uncommitted changes.
